chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who prostrates while wearing a turban, and his face does not touch the ground. He (peace be upon him) said: 'That does not suffice him until his forehead touches the ground.'

key_terms.لَا يُجْزِئُهُ: does not suffice him / is not valid

ai.seo_question: Does wearing a turban invalidate the prostration in prayer if the forehead does not touch the ground?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the validity of prostration (*sujdah*) is contingent upon the forehead (*jibha*) touching the ground, regardless of whether one is wearing a turban (*imamah*). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the physical contact of the specific body part mentioned in the Quran, distinguishing it from mere facial proximity, and highlights the practical application of ritual purity and completeness in prayer.
